revision_summary: No quote fabrications were found (all quotes match transcript text), and the overall outcome classification (no_appointment, dead-end referral call) is well-supported and should be preserved. However, Stage 3 needs one targeted revision: it must explicitly flag that this transcript's speaker diarization is unreliable for large stretches of the call. Evidence: 'Yes. This is he.' (00:03) and 'Give me a minute' (00:41) and the real-time phone-number correction exchange at 02:11-02:24 ('2402402996381' followed by 'what?' and '81.') are all tagged 'rep' but are clearly two-way exchanges or the other party's lines. Stage 3 built its entire trajectory narrative (starting_state, state_changes, cherry_pick_moments, coaching_focus) on these labels without caveat. On rerun: (1) add an explicit confidence caveat in trajectory_verdict or starting_state noting the diarization is unreliable and that the 'Walter vs. neighbor' and dead-air readings are best-effort given mislabeled turns; (2) reconsider the two state_changes entries (00:10 and 01:47) that depend on attributing specific lines to specific speakers with unwarranted confidence; (3) correct the schema_reference for the 00:22 cherry_pick_moment away from friction_resolution_speed (defined narrowly around contact-frequency/harassment complaints) to a better fit or null; (4) consider using analysis_directives.time_burn_detection as the schema_reference for the CRM-lookup-delay moment instead of leaving it null. These are calibration fixes, not a full rerun -- the core outcome read and coaching priorities (own the referral lead directly, tighten CRM lookup speed) remain valid and should be kept.
